title: Appliance Rebates in Niagara Falls 2026: Up to $200 Per Appliance
desc: Niagara Falls appliance rebates for 2026: $25 to $200 from Home Renovation Savings, with Niagara Peninsula Energy as distributor.
lead: Niagara Falls has 37,795 households, 66% of them in detached homes, and 61% live in homes built before 1981.
cards_heading: What Ontario pays for new appliances in Niagara Falls
cards_intro: We re-read the program's appliance page on October 4, 2026. The rebates are province-wide, so the amounts are the same in every city, and the rules about what you replace and which model you buy are what decide a claim.

cards.title: Heat pump clothes dryer
cards.note: The largest of the six appliance rebates, for a new ENERGY STAR Most Efficient heat pump dryer replacing an electric dryer.

cards.title: Induction cooktop or range
cards.note: For a new induction cooktop or range on the program's product list, replacing an existing electric one.

cards.title: Washing machine
cards.note: For a new ENERGY STAR Most Efficient washer on the program list.

cards.title: Fridge
cards.note: For a new ENERGY STAR Most Efficient refrigerator replacing an existing electric one.

cards.title: Freezer
cards.note: For a new ENERGY STAR Most Efficient freezer on the list.

cards.title: Dishwasher
cards.note: For a new ENERGY STAR Most Efficient dishwasher on the list.

cards.title: Who can claim
cards.note: A residential customer on the Ontario grid with an existing electric appliance in need of replacing. Cornwall Electric customers are excluded.

cards.title: Free route
cards.note: Income-qualified households can get energy-efficient fridges and freezers at no charge, along with other upgrades.

after_cards: The appliance page states no end date, so confirm it is still open before you buy.
sections: 70% of households own and only 4% live in tall buildings. The appliance rebate fits a house where one appliance fails at a time. 61% of the city's homes were built before 1981, though the age of the house says little about the age of its fridge.
Niagara Peninsula Energy is the distributor, and Niagara Falls postal codes begin with L, which the Energy Affordability Program lists. January lows average -6.1°C, the mildest of the 25 cities.
Buy new, then upload the receipt

Buy a new appliance from any retailer, then upload the receipt on the program page within 60 days of purchase. Used and refurbished units do not qualify. Keep the receipt, the model number and the delivery date together. Niagara Falls households who buy during a sale should still confirm the model is on the list at the time they check out.

The program page asks for an existing electric appliance in need of replacing. A new fridge to go in a spare corner, or an induction range where the kitchen had no range, is not a replacement. If you are switching from gas to an electric appliance, the page does not say whether that counts, so ask the program before you buy. Niagara Falls households that already cook on an electric range are the clearest fit for the induction rebate.
Fridges and freezers at no cost

The Energy Affordability Program lists energy-efficient refrigerators and freezers among the items that comprehensive support can provide, along with LED bulbs, dehumidifiers and window air conditioners. It does not list washers or dryers, and its saving kits include no major appliances. Income limits run from $48,220 for one person to $96,439 for four, and Niagara Falls postal codes are among those it covers. Call 1-844-770-3148 to ask.

Unlike the thermostat rebate, the appliance page lists no home type. It asks for a residential customer on the Ontario grid. It does not address condos or apartments directly, so a Niagara Falls condo owner or tenant should confirm with the program. 30% of Niagara Falls households rent, and a tenant should ask the landlord before swapping a fridge or range that came with the unit.
claim_heading: How to claim in Niagara Falls
claim_steps: Check that the appliance you are replacing is electric and that you are on the Ontario grid.
Find a new model on the program's ENERGY STAR Most Efficient list for that appliance.
Buy it new from any retailer and keep the receipt.
Upload the receipt on the program page within 60 days of purchase.
If your household income is under the limits, call 1-844-770-3148 about free fridges and freezers first.
faq: Does Niagara Peninsula Energy give an appliance rebate?
Can I claim for a seasonal property?
The page asks for a residential customer on the Ontario grid. Ask about seasonal use.
